title: RESOLVER NOT OK (NOT CONNECTED?)
symptoms: Machine resolver signal is not detected correctly.
steps: Apply plant LOTO before opening electrical enclosures or disconnecting resolver wiring.
Inspect cable #52 and both connector ends for looseness, contamination, damaged pins or cable damage.
Check resolver and its wiring against the resolver information in the wiring manual.
If wiring and resolver are satisfactory, continue diagnosis at the MCB rather than replacing boards by trial.

title: CHECK RESOLVER CONNECTIONS
symptoms: Machine cannot reliably detect resolver/signals.
steps: Inspect cable #52 and connectors.
Check resolver wiring and resolver condition.
Check the MCB-side connection and diagnostics.

title: SPEED MONITORING: STARTING IS TAKING TOO LONG
symptoms: Machine does not reach expected speed during starting.
steps: Check for mechanical overload before electrical replacement.
Check resolver signal, setting and cable #52.
Review DDMP/main-drive diagnostics.
Check motor and drive only after wiring and mechanical load are excluded.
keywords: starting too long speed sumo motor ddmp

title: ACP: RESYNCHRONIZATION REQUIRED
symptoms: Pick-finder position is not in the required position.
steps: Use the prescribed PFF/PFR action from the machine message.
Check PX-PP/PX-WP sensing and mechanical target position.
Inspect cables #174/#175 and MCB inputs.
keywords: acp resynchronization pff pfr pxpp pxwp pick finder

title: EMERGENCY STOP PRESSED
drawingRefs: Button safety logic — Wiring PDF pp129–130
symptoms: Safety chain reports emergency-stop condition.
steps: Do not bypass the safety chain.
Identify and reset the operated E-stop only after the machine is safe.
If the message remains, inspect the E-stop circuit and second-contact safety logic using the referenced drawings.

title: DDMP BOARD NOT CONNECTED
symptoms: MCB does not detect the DDMP board.
steps: Isolate power according to plant procedure.
Check DDMP seating and connections.
Inspect MCB–DDMP interconnection.
Use board diagnostics before substituting DDMP or MCB.

title: SUMO: MAIN MOTOR CONTROL / SWITCHED OFF
symptoms: Main motor control reports switched-off condition.
steps: Check for accompanying SUMO or supply messages.
Inspect DDMP and drive diagnostic LEDs.
Check optical communication and relevant supplies.
Do not replace drive electronics until motor and wiring checks are complete.
keywords: sumo main motor switched off ldec powerbox

title: IPS (PWR) POWER FAILS
symptoms: PWR supply status is low/not OK.
steps: Check for short circuit/overload before replacing a board.
Check IPS indications and supply outputs.
Trace the supply through EPDAF to the MCB using the power-supply drawings.

title: IPS (DC-OK) NO VOLTAGE
symptoms: DC-OK status is not present.
steps: Check IPS DC-OK indication.
Check for supply short/overload.
Inspect the IPS–EPDAF connection and supply outputs before board replacement.

title: 26VDC5 FAILS
symptoms: 26VDC5 is below the expected monitoring threshold.
steps: Measure the control supply safely at the documented test points.
Check the +26 V distribution for a short or excessive load.
Trace IPS/EPDAF to MCB before replacing the MCB.

title: 26VDC FAILS / CHECK FUSES
symptoms: +26 V control supply is missing or protected circuit has opened.
steps: Find and correct any short before replacing a fuse.
Check EPDAF fuse/LED indications.
Measure +26 V along the documented distribution path.

title: CHECK 5V
symptoms: 5 V control supply is not correct.
steps: Check +5 V using the documented circuit and safe measurement practice.
Inspect related supply wiring and connectors.
Resolve upstream supply faults before suspecting the MCB.

title: PREWINDER COMMUNICATION ERROR / INTERFERENCE
symptoms: Communication with a prewinder channel is disturbed.
steps: Check PICAN connectors and cable condition.
Check bus termination; the wiring manual describes 120-ohm end termination.
Use the display PICAN device information to identify the affected channel/device.
keywords: prewinder pican communication interference can bus

title: ETU: TEMPERATURE MOTOR TOO HIGH
symptoms: ETU motor thermal contact indicates excessive temperature.
steps: Allow the motor to cool and determine why it overheated before restarting.
Check take-up mechanism for abnormal load.
Check motor, resolver/brake wiring and TRIAX diagnostics.
Review operating demand/pick density if the mechanical system is normal.
keywords: etu temperature hot take up triax motor

title: CHECK THE ETU
symptoms: ETU drive or motor error.
steps: Check for accompanying TRIAX/ETU message.
Inspect ETU mechanical load.
Check motor, resolver and brake connections.
Use TRIAX diagnostics before replacing components.

title: CHECK TSW WARP TENSION SENSOR (TSF)
symptoms: Warp-tension sensor test fails or tension is detected too low for an ELO action.
steps: Check sensor mounting and freedom of movement.
Check sensor connection and wiring.
Verify zero adjustment with the warp in the required condition.
Check the MCB input only after sensor/mechanical checks.
keywords: tsw tsf warp tension sensor elo

title: TSF SENSOR 1: ZERO ADJUSTMENT NOT POSSIBLE
symptoms: Zero adjustment of warp-tension sensor cannot be completed.
steps: Put the machine/warp in the manual-prescribed condition for zeroing.
Check sensor mechanical freedom and connection.
Repeat zero adjustment.
If unsuccessful, trace sensor wiring to MCB.

title: WARP TENSION TOO HIGH
symptoms: Measured warp tension exceeds the upper limit.
steps: First determine whether the tension is physically high or the sensor reading is wrong.
Check sensor and zero/reference condition.
Inspect let-off mechanics/gearing for restriction.
Check ELO motor/TRIAX only after mechanical and sensor checks.

title: WARP TENSION UNATTAINABLE
symptoms: Nominal warp tension cannot be reached.
steps: Inspect beam and let-off mechanism for abnormal movement or restriction.
Check gearing/setup.
Check ELO motor, resolver/brake wiring and TRIAX diagnostics.
Escalate to control/MCB only after mechanical and drive checks.
keywords: warp tension unattainable elo let off

title: CHECK ELO
drawingRefs: TRIAX control box — Wiring PDF pp82–86
symptoms: ELO drive/motor error.
steps: Check for accompanying TRIAX message.
Inspect let-off mechanical load.
Check ELO motor, resolver and brake cables.
Use TRIAX diagnostics before component replacement.
keywords: check elo electronic let off triax

title: DOBBY: COMMUNICATION FAILS
symptoms: CAN/PICAN communication with dobby fails.
steps: Inspect PICAN/CAN cable and connectors.
Verify end termination according to the wiring manual.
Check interface/controller status and configuration.
Check MCB communication only after bus wiring is verified.

title: JACQUARD: COMMUNICATION ERROR
symptoms: Communication with Jacquard controller/interface fails.
steps: Check PICAN/CAN wiring and connectors.
Verify termination for the Jacquard configuration.
Check configured type/production data and controller/interface status.
Check MCB communication after bus-side checks.

title: UNDERVOLTAGE
symptoms: TRIAX detects low DC-bus voltage.
steps: Use qualified electrical personnel for DC-bus measurements.
Check the 290 VDC supply and documented protection path.
Inspect wiring/connectors to TRIAX.
Only suspect TRIAX after supply integrity is proven.

title: MOTOR OVERHEATED
symptoms: Motor thermal contact indicates overtemperature.
steps: Allow motor to cool and find the overload cause.
Inspect mechanical load.
Check thermal-contact and motor wiring.
Check TRIAX diagnostics.

title: MOTOR CURRENT FAILURE
symptoms: Drive detects a motor phase/current problem.
steps: Isolate power before resistance/continuity checks.
Check motor phase wiring and connections.
Check motor winding condition.
Do not replace TRIAX before motor and cable faults are excluded.

title: BRAKE CURRENT NOT OK
symptoms: Expected brake current is not detected.
steps: Check brake connector and cable.
Check brake coil according to the applicable motor circuit.
Check TRIAX output/diagnostics after the brake circuit is verified.

title: MOTOR OVERLOAD
symptoms: TRIAX detects excessive motor load.
steps: Check mechanical load first.
Inspect motor and resolver wiring.
Check motor condition.
Use TRIAX diagnostics before board replacement.

title: POSITION CONTROL ERROR
symptoms: Motor position deviation exceeds the permitted value.
steps: Check for E-stop/safety interruption.
Inspect motor and resolver wiring.
Check resolver/mechanical coupling.
Use TRIAX diagnostics to distinguish drive from motor/resolver fault.

title: RESOLVER NOT OK
symptoms: TRIAX does not receive a valid motor resolver signal.
steps: Inspect resolver cable/connectors.
Check resolver according to the wiring manual.
Check TRIAX connection/diagnostics only after resolver circuit checks.

title: MCB MACHINE STOP PROTECTION — CHECK DTKMM
drawingRefs: HV/main motor — Wiring PDF pp31 onward
symptoms: MCB machine-stop protection detects unexpected KMM switching/status.
steps: Keep the machine isolated while inspecting contactor circuitry.
Check KMM and associated wiring/status signal.
Trace the HV/control path using the referenced mains drawings.
Check MCB detection after contactor/wiring checks.
keywords: dtkmm kmm machine stop protection mcb

title: DANGER! UNEXPECTED MOVEMENT — CHECK MACHINE BRAKE
symptoms: Control detects a condition associated with unexpected movement.
steps: Treat this as a safety-critical fault; do not operate the machine until resolved.
Inspect machine brake mechanically and electrically.
Check resolver/cable feedback.
Verify the safety/detection circuit before returning the machine to service.

title: SUMO SWITCHED OFF
symptoms: SUMO/powerbox reports switched-off state.
steps: Check for accompanying drive-disable, supply or powerbox messages.
Inspect DDMP and drive diagnostics.
Check relevant safety/drive-enable wiring.
Resolve motor/wiring faults before replacing power electronics.

title: SUMO COMMUNICATION TIMEOUT
symptoms: Communication between MCB/DDMP and main-motor drive times out.
steps: Check optical cable seating/condition and avoid tight bends.
Check DDMP and drive diagnostic indications.
Verify power to the involved modules.
Substitute boards only after communication and supply checks.
keywords: sumo communication timeout optical ddmp ldec

title: SUMO: CHECK PXWP / PXPP
symptoms: PX-WP/PX-PP signals are conflicting or unexpected.
steps: Check sensor targets and physical adjustment.
Inspect cables #174/#175 and connectors.
Check MCB input indication for both sensors.
Correct sensing before attempting drive resynchronization.

title: SUMO RESYNCHRONIZATION FAILED — PHASE(S) FAILED
symptoms: Main-drive resynchronization detects failed motor phase(s).
steps: Isolate the machine before motor resistance/insulation tests.
Check phase connections, phase resistance and insulation to earth according to the manual.
Use the drive/manual diagnostic procedure to distinguish motor from drive fault.
Do not fit a replacement power board to a suspect motor circuit.

title: SUMO / MAIN MOTOR CONTROL LOW VOLTAGE TOO LOW
symptoms: Main motor control reports insufficient low/control voltage.
steps: Check incoming/control supply and contactor state.
Inspect inrush/supply circuit and drive indications.
Correct supply fault before drive-board replacement.
keywords: sumo low voltage too low kmm inrush

title: SUMO MAIN MOTOR CONTROL — NO COMMUNICATION
symptoms: No communication with main motor control.
steps: Verify the drive has its required power and no upstream protection has opened.
Inspect optical communication cable and connectors.
Check DDMP and drive LEDs/diagnostics.
Only then consider module substitution.
keywords: sumo no communication ldec ddmp optical

title: SUMO MAIN MOTOR CONTROL — COMMUNICATION FAILS
symptoms: Communication between DDMP and main motor control fails.
steps: Check drive power and protection status.
Inspect optical cable and connections.
Check DDMP and LDEC/powerbox diagnostic indications.
Check supply/inrush path before board replacement.
keywords: sumo communication fails optical ddmp ldec

title: SUMO MAIN MOTOR CONTROL — UNDERVOLTAGE
symptoms: Main motor powerbox DC link is below its permitted level.
steps: Qualified personnel only: check incoming three-phase supply and documented protection/contactor path.
Check powerbox status indicators.
Do not work on the DC link until discharge and LOTO requirements are satisfied.

title: SUMO POWERBOX OVERVOLTAGE
symptoms: Powerbox detects excessive DC-link voltage.
steps: Check incoming mains voltage against the machine supply specification.
Inspect the documented powerbox/resistor circuit and diagnostic indications.
Do not replace power electronics until supply conditions are verified.

title: SUMO POWERBOX VLSOK VOLTAGE FAILURE
symptoms: Powerbox control-voltage/status signal is missing.
steps: Check the documented control-voltage/status wiring.
Inspect PDAF/EPDAF and powerbox connections.
Check module diagnostics before replacement.

title: SUMO MAIN MOTOR CONTROL SWITCHED OFF (DTSC)
symptoms: Main motor control reports DTSC switched-off condition.
steps: Check accompanying SUMO messages and drive diagnostics.
Check motor phase circuit before replacing drive electronics.
Follow the manual SUMO test/diagnostic path for the installed drive version.
keywords: dtsc sumo switched off main motor
